advanced.title: Advanced options
advanced.subtitle: Carefully chosen defaults — adjust only if needed.
advanced.customVoiceHint: Narrates the lessons with YOUR voice (sample recorded in Settings → My voice, with consent). Otherwise, an automatic synthetic voice suited to the course language.
advanced.voiceCatalogHint: ONE voice for the whole course: the chosen identity is pinned across every video, whatever the engine. Default: {default}.
advanced.ttsEngineHint: The engine used for standard narration and voice cloning. Can be changed later, lesson by lesson, from the "Repair audio" button.
advanced.themeHint: Palette and mood of video slides and articles. Changeable later from the course page (videos are re-rendered).
advanced.imageEngineHint: The model used for course and slide illustrations. Can be changed later, slide by slide, from its image panel.
advanced.platformsHint: Exports (formats, thumbnails) adapt to each platform.
advanced.avatarHint: A talking-head presenter introduces and closes each section. With a PHOTO of your face (Settings → My avatar), a Ditto render is animated over the narration; otherwise a HeyGen avatar (paid plans) or a title card as fallback.
advanced.avatarSelectHint: Used only if no presenter photo is saved. With a photo (Settings → My avatar), the Ditto avatar animated over your face takes priority.
advanced.clonedVoiceHint: Narrates the course with your custom voice (Chatterbox). Requires a voice sample recorded in Settings → My voice; otherwise the standard voice is used.
advanced.offPeakHint: Starts during off-peak hours (2–6 AM) — next slot {day} at {time}.
advanced.sectionsRange: Between {min} and {max} — the AI adjusts to the topic.
advanced.sourceUnsupported: Unsupported format — PDF, PPTX or Markdown expected.
advanced.sourceChoose: Choose a PDF, PPTX or Markdown file
advanced.sourceHint: The course outline will draw on this content (progression, vocabulary, examples).
advanced.genFinalExamHint: Adds a recap exam at the end of the course.
advanced.genContentRatioHint: 4 weights separated by commas — e.g. “40,25,20,15”. Empty = default balance.
advanced.genAudienceHint: E.g. “Moroccan accountants discovering Excel” — adapts examples and vocabulary.
advanced.genSpacedRepetitionHint: Reintroduces key concepts from earlier sections into later quizzes.
advanced.genCertificationTargetHint: Aligns content and quizzes with the official framework.
advanced.genGlossaryHint: Terminology to follow word for word throughout the course (max 2000 characters).
advanced.genSlideLanguageHint: Slides in a language different from the narration (e.g. EN slides, FR voice).
advanced.genVerticalHint: Also generates a shorts-format version (TikTok/Reels/YouTube Shorts).
advanced.genDialogueHint: Narration as a trainer/learner dialogue — more engaging, read by two distinct voices.
advanced.genValAfterScriptsHint: In “step-by-step validation” mode, it stops after the video script (before voice synthesis) — you review it, then launch the voice, which avoids regenerating the audio. The outline is always reviewed before generation anyway.
advanced.genValAfterDraftHint: Stops after a practical-work draft (before the costly Playwright screenshots) — you review/edit the exercise, then relaunch the capture. No effect on videos/articles/quizzes.

faq.title: Frequently asked questions
faq.subtitle: Everything you need to know before you start.

items.question: How does course generation work?
items.answer: You provide a title and difficulty level: SallyCourse automatically generates the outline, lessons, articles, video scripts, quizzes and related resources.

items.question: Can I deploy to multiple platforms?
items.answer: Yes, depending on your plan you can deploy simultaneously to Udemy, YouTube, Teachable, Thinkific, Podia, Gumroad, Skillshare and other SCORM-compatible platforms.

items.question: Is the generated content unique?
items.answer: Each course is generated from your title and preferences, producing original content tailored to your topic.

items.question: Can I edit the generated course?
items.answer: Yes, every lesson, quiz and resource remains editable before publishing from your dashboard.

items.question: What happens if I change plans?
items.answer: You can change plans at any time; your existing courses remain available and new limits apply immediately.

resilience.subtitle: Degraded mode: state of the worker's circuit breakers (automatic switch to a fallback when an external provider is down) and multi-platform deployment isolation.

empty.title: No breaker recorded
empty.description: Breakers appear as soon as they first change state (e.g. the first ElevenLabs failure). No entry here means no incident has been detected yet.

resilience.fallbackNote: Configured fallback: ElevenLabs voice synthesis → OpenAI TTS (5 consecutive failures open the circuit, retry after 60s). Claude calls: local queue with increasing back-off on repeated 429s (1s/2s/4s/8s), without any new infrastructure.
resilience.deploymentBody: Each platform (Udemy, YouTube, Podia, …) is handled by an independent BullMQ job on the deployment queue (one job = one course/platform pair). If a platform fails, only its own job fails — the other jobs in the same deployment wave are neither blocked nor cancelled (native queue isolation). Detailed per-platform status: see the jobs.

compare.note: OSS cost = Hetzner compute only (ffmpeg/ollama/piper CPU-hours at {rate}/h), no per-token/character billing. Recommendation: rare language or business plan → cloud for the plan/scripts (llm), OSS for the rest; otherwise fully OSS. cache.heading: Cache

ops.title: Ops
ops.subtitle: Live provider credits, server resources, queue throughput, and real per-provider call latency (including Modal) — three blind spots found during the 2026-07-29 video/voice quality audit.

alerts.creditsTitle: Provider(s) to watch (low or exhausted credit):

sections.creditsNote: DeepSeek and Moonshot expose an exact balance (dedicated API). Other providers are probed live (minimal call): "operational" does not guarantee a healthy balance, only that a call succeeded less than 15 minutes ago.

server.unreachableDescription: The worker metrics server (internal network) did not respond — server figures are temporarily unavailable. The rest of the dashboard (credits, costs) is unaffected.

timing.emptyDescription: Provider call timing (TTS, image, transcription, cloud LLM) was added on 2026-07-29 — earlier CostRecord rows do not have it. Data will appear as new generations run.
timing.note: P95 = 95% of calls are faster than this value (highlights slow outliers, notably Modal cold-starts). "Timed calls" may be lower than the provider's total call count if some predate this addition.

motion.title: Motion
motion.lead: Five durations, four curves, three entrances: a short, strict vocabulary. Micro-interactions stay under 250 ms; the spring is reserved for celebrations. prefers-reduced-motion is always respected.
motion.durationsNote: Each marble runs the same distance: only the duration changes. In RTL, the race reverses naturally (movement uses a logical margin).
motion.easingsNote: Watch the spring overshoot its target slightly before settling — reserve it for moments of celebration.

illustrations.lead: A language of “flow”: the prompt’s spark travels through violet currents and materializes into structured knowledge. Abstract geometry, 1.5 px strokes, gold as punctuation only — never a solid fill.

fluxCours.name: Prompt → course flow
fluxCours.title: A spark unfolds into three currents that become course modules

constellation.name: Constellation
constellation.title: A graph of concepts linked around a golden node

strates.name: Knowledge strata
strates.title: Isometric layers crossed by a rising golden thread

etincelle.label: Spark — punctuation motif
etincelle.title: SALISTAR spark
etincelle.description: Four concave branches, gold on a violet circle. Use as a list marker, a celebration accent or a discreet signature — one per screen is enough.

strokes.desc: — 1.5 px, round caps, violet 400/500 at 30–70% opacity.

gradient.desc: — violet → gold reserved for trajectories and borders, never as a fill.

gold.desc: — a single golden focal point per illustration: the idea, the course, the achievement.

palette.title: Palette
palette.lead: Seven 50→950 scales derived from tokens.ts — brand violet, premium gold, warm violet-tinted neutrals and four harmonised states. Clicking a swatch copies its hex; the gold ring marks the brand shade.

violet.label: Violet — primary
violet.usage: Actions, links, identity. #5B2A86 set at shade 700.

neutral.label: Warm neutrals
neutral.usage: Text, borders, surfaces — violet-tinted, never cold grey. Brand background #0D0714 at shade 950.

roles.heading: Semantic roles (vary with the theme — toggle light/dark above)

typography.title: Typography
typography.lead: Fraunces embodies the editorial voice, Figtree carries the reading, IBM Plex Sans Arabic handles Arabic on its own — headings and body. A modular scale with a 1.25 ratio sets the rhythm throughout.

specimenArabic.label: Arabic — IBM Plex Sans Arabic (headings and body, never italic)

scale.label: Modular scale — 1.25 ratio (major fourth), 16 px base

pairing.label: Pairing rules
pairing.item2: AR: headings AND body in font-arabic — weight ≥ 600 for headings, never serif or italic.
pairing.item3: Mixed text: the family follows the block's dominant language, and fallbacks cover occasional insertions from the other script.

section.title: Spacing · Radii · Shadows
section.lead: A 4 px grid with no exceptions (well, almost), three structural radii, and shadows tinted with deep violet: the quiet material that holds every screen together.

spacing.label: Spacing — strict 4 px grid (only exception: 2 px)

radii.label: Radii — three structural steps (8 / 12 / 16) + xl and pill

shadows.label: Shadows — always violet-tinted, never pure black
shadows.note: In dark theme, shadows fade in favor of edges and glows: switch to light to read the full depth of the scale.

styleguide.heroTitle:
The studio where every

idea becomes a course.
styleguide.heroDescription: Deep dark backgrounds tinted with purple, gold in rare touches, frosted glass and film grain: SallyCourse borrows its codes from high-end production studios. This living guide is its reference — observe every foundation in light, dark and RTL.
styleguide.heroIllustrationTitle: Flow illustration: from a spark of a prompt, the modules of a course are born

header.title: Motion & micro-interactions
header.intro: SALISTAR motion communicates a state — entry, progress, success, interactivity. Durations and curves come from tokens; everything respects prefers-reduced-motion.
header.transitionNote: — navigating between the two pages replays the page transition (fade + slide 200 ms via template.tsx).

timeline.cardDescription: The rail fills as the steps progress; the active step pulses while the system works; completion triggers the celebration.

next.title: Next.js App Router from A to Z

default.title: 2° tilt (default)
default.description: Hover: the card follows the pointer with a soft spring — enough to signal interactivity, never enough to distract.

exaggerated.title: 6° tilt (exaggerated)
exaggerated.description: Amplified version to make the effect legible in the demo — do NOT use in production: 2° is enough.

tokens.reducedMotion: prefers-reduced-motion active: translations are neutralized, only fades remain.
tokens.durations: Token durations: instant {instant} ms · fast {fast} ms · base {base} ms · slow {slow} ms · slower {slower} ms — entry curve out [{easing}].

timeline.title: Generation timeline
timeline.intent: Progress of a long process: the rail fills organically, the active step pulses, success triggers a spring checkmark + confetti, failure freezes the rail.

stagger.title: Orchestrated lists (stagger)
stagger.intent: The staggered appearance of the cards communicates the reading order of a course grid — triggered on entering the viewport.

countup.title: Animated counters
countup.intent: The statistics "count up" when they come into view: tabular figures (no jitter), localized formatting, direct final value in reduced motion.

tilt.title: Subtle 3D tilt
tilt.intent: The ±2° tilt that follows the pointer signals that a card is interactive — disabled on touch and in reduced motion.

transitions.title: Reference transitions
transitions.intent: The five transitions named by intent (enter, exit, state, springSoft, springSnappy) applied to the same fade-in-up variant, to compare their temperaments.

header.title: SALISTAR Components
header.description: SallyCourse UI library: every component is shown in all its states — dark mode by default, native RTL, understated animations.
